title: Sort machined blocks with a go/no-go gap gauge: let go of each block on the gap and tray it by whether it drops in
instruction: Check each of the six aluminium blocks on the gauge, setting it on the green GO gap and, only if it drops in, then on the red NO-GO gap. Put each block that drops into GO but not into NO-GO in the green tray and every other block in the red tray.
context: Checking parts against fixed-limit gauges and rejecting those out of specification is core work for inspectors, testers, sorters, samplers and weighers, about 600,000 US workers. A block is set on the GO gap, where it must drop in, and if it does, on the NO-GO gap, where it must not. It is let go there because a fixed gap gauge reads by the part's own weight: a held part can be forced in or held off. The nearest passing and failing blocks differ by 2.2 mm in width, and which block starts where changes with the layout. Unlike measuring a part with calipers and reading a value, nothing is read here: the fixed gaps decide, and the robot must set each block down squarely, let go, take it again from wherever it came to rest, and act on whether it dropped in. Unlike plain sorting into bins, the right tray is unknown until the block has been tried on the gauge, and a block earns credit only after that check.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases on the table top: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up. Blocks (loose, 6): bare aluminium, 6.0 long (x) x 2.0 tall, widths (y) A 3.93, B 3.95, C 3.97, D 3.71, E 3.68, F 4.19 (specified 4.00 +- 0.13, so A, B, C are in tolerance), density 2700 kg/m3 (119 to 136 g), letters on the undersides. They lie flat, long side along x, at six start places x 18, 28, 38 at y +23 and y -23; GAUGE_SORT_LAYOUT (default 0) shuffles which block is where. Gauge (fixed, steel): base plate 5.0 (x) x 17.0 (y) x 1.0 centred at x 32, y 0. On it two gaps across y, each between two anvils 1.0 (x) x 1.2 (y) x 1.5 tall at x 32: GO gap 4.13 wide centred at y +4.5 (green anvils), NO-GO gap 3.87 wide at y -4.5 (red anvils); each anvil's inner top edge has a 0.2 x 45 degree lead-in chamfer; gauge friction 0.4. A seated block stands 0.5 above the anvil tops; a block that must drop in clears the gap by at least 0.08 a side, one that must stay out overlaps each anvil by at least 0.03. Trays (fixed): green at x 17, y +9 and red at x 17, y -9, inside 12 (x) x 16 (y), 0.4 floor, walls 3.0 tall and 0.6 thick. Friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic (the station's default for task objects). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A block earns credit only if it was checked, in order, and ends in the tray its checks call for. A check at a gap counts when, for 6 control steps in a row (0.3 s at 20 Hz): every gripper whose TCP (the point between the finger pads, 13 mm short of their tips) is within 5 cm of the block is open wider than 6.5 cm (finger joints read from the simulator); the gauge (base plus that gap's anvils) pushes up on the block, normal plus friction, with at least 0.8 of its weight and the robot pushes on it with at most 0.02 N (PhysX contact forces); and the pose shows a reading, with the block's long side along the gap's slot: seated (level, on the base between the anvils) = drops in; stays out = not seated but resting on the anvils, level or tipped against one up to 30 degrees, centre over the gap, lowest point at most 1.5 mm above the anvil tops (the force condition is what shows the gauge carries it). A reading the block's width does not allow (a narrow block perched across the gap) is no reading. NO-GO counts only after a GO 'drops in'; the first reading at each gap stands. Drops into GO and stays out of NO-GO = green tray; stays out of GO, or drops into NO-GO = red tray. In a tray: footprint inside the walls, still, released (same gripper rule), and resting on the floor or on a block that is itself in that tray. Score = blocks credited / 6, capped at 0.25 if any out-of-tolerance block is anywhere over the green tray's outer footprint (in it, on its rim, or held above it). If forces cannot be read no check counts; if the grippers cannot be read, or the control rate is not 20 Hz, no check counts and no block is in a tray, so the trial scores 0. Checks reset at every trial reset. Real trial, from the uninterrupted video: follow each block from its known start place; a check counts when that block is seen left alone on the gap, gripper visibly open and clear, for at least 0.3 s (6 frames of the 20 frames-per-second video); trays are read at the end.
reset_notes: Run with -E object_jitter=0 -E control_hz=20. Lay the six blocks flat, long side front to back, at their start places for the chosen layout (GAUGE_SORT_LAYOUT; the README lists them); empty both trays.
fidelity: Rigid boxes. The tolerance is scaled up from real gauging practice: real fixed-limit gauges work to hundredths of a millimetre; here blocks clear a gap by at least 0.8 mm a side or overlap its anvils by at least 0.3 mm a side, the tightest margins that rigid contacts and the arms' positioning resolved reliably. Anvils have a 2 mm lead-in chamfer. Friction: blocks 1.2, gauge 0.4. Gauge support counts normal and friction contact force at the last physics substep of each control step.
